name: Mills Hall

facts.text: Dedicated November 7, 2002 and named for Eugene Mills, UNH president 1975-1979, who later led Whittier College.

Suite-style hall for sophomores and upper-class students: four- to eight-person suites with their own bathrooms, larger suites with common rooms, five floors with two or three lounges each, and a seminar room.
Has air conditioning and an elevator; 358 students at 20 Quad Way, next to the MUB.

verdict: 2002 neo-Georgian suite hall with A/C and private baths next to the MUB; upper-class students' favourite.
notes: Photo 02 is tagged PD-self by an uploader naming the engineering firm Vanderweil as author, with no VRT permission on file; its public-domain status is doubtful, so prefer 01. Both photos show a five-storey red-brick neo-Georgian block with stone-banded floors, gabled pavilions with lunette windows and chimneys. It is handsome and well kept, but plain. Contradiction: the Housing page says Mills was president 1971-1974; the archives say acting president from July 1974 and president 1975-1979. The archives are more likely right. Architect and builder were not confirmed from a page I opened (a search snippet cited JSA Inc. and Gilbane from a 2002 UNH release I could not open). No interior photos.
judgeNotes: Photo shows a handsome, well-kept but generic brick block. Dropped 02.jpg: its public-domain tag is doubtful (no permission on file).
